entries.title: Citation cards jump to each citing paragraph
entries.body: The card for a cited work, opened from the reference list or from a citation in the text, lists the paragraphs that cite it, numbered in the order they appear. Choose one to jump there, with the citing words highlighted. A long list shows the first 20 and then how many more, and the card says "at least" when some later citations may not be counted.

entries.title: One logo while an article loads
entries.body: While an article is loading, the page shows just the spinning Spideryarn logo in the middle, instead of a second logo in the corner as well.

entries.title: Unsent recordings return only where you made them
entries.body: A spoken recording you had not sent could be offered back in the wrong place, such as another article's "Why you're reading this one" box or a different chat. Each recording now comes back only in the box it was made in. Pointing at the microphone also explains what it is for and how to send with it.

entries.title: Every arXiv paper version is one article
entries.body: Adding an arXiv paper by its plain link, when you already had a numbered version of it, gave you the paper twice. Every version of a paper is now treated as the same article, including ones already in your library. More of the tracking tags added to links are also ignored, so they no longer make a second copy.

entries.title: arXiv papers open with cleaner text
entries.body: Newly added arXiv papers could start with one run-together paragraph of author details and stray labels, sometimes losing an author, or with leftover typesetting commands in the text. Authors, contact details and thanks notes are now laid out separately and kept whole, and the stray commands are removed without touching the maths.

entries.title: Cut-off chat answers stay marked after reloading
entries.body: When a chat answer was cut short, the warning saying so disappeared once you reloaded the page, so the answer looked complete. The warning is now kept. With the more capable AI switched on, chat answers and explanations of a passage also have more room before they are cut off.

entries.title: A failed web search is not repeated blindly
entries.body: When a request that searches the web lost its connection partway, it was sent again automatically, so the same paid search could run more than once. It is now sent again only when it clearly never left. Otherwise you may see an error instead, and can try again yourself.
